_about: E2 recall harness fixtures (S291, 2026-09-01). A fictional workshop world:
machines Anvil (Linux laptop) and Bellows (Windows workstation), agents Pip
and Quill, an owner, and the doctrines/incidents/decisions of a small
fleet. Nothing here is a real memory; the store under test is a fresh
tmp store, so the only thing measured is the ranker's geometry.
memories: id, summary (the embedded text), category, age_days (created_at
= now - age), access_count (recall_stats seed). Decoys are memories that
share words or topic with a query but are the WRONG answer.
queries: id, prompt, expected (ids that count as a hit), note. recall@5 =
|expected in top-5| / |expected|; MRR = 1 / rank of the first expected id.
gate: measured floors, never tuned to pass. Floor = the first honest run
(recall@5 0.9714, MRR 0.9010, 35 queries, 2026-09-01, ranker E1) minus one
full query miss (1/35), so one rank moving is churn and two queries lost
is a regression. Re-baseline only with a ranker change that the report
shows improving; write the new measured values here when you do.
hard: true marks the queries where the first honest run did NOT serve the
answer at rank 1 (q06/q08/q13/q19/q33) plus the multi-hit q14 — the cases
that discriminate. The primary floors average 35 queries, so a regression
on these six can hide behind the easy majority (Opie, #3167). gate.
hard_mrr_min floors MRR over that subset alone; headroom = one rank step
at the top (rr 1.0 -> 0.5) on one hard query = 0.5 / 6, finer than the
primary's one-query headroom, which on this subset is the same as the
primary gate and therefore adds nothing.
First honest hard-subset run: MRR 0.4222 (6 queries, 2026-09-02, ranker E1,
same serving as the primary baseline) minus 0.0833 = 0.338.
SECOND BASELINE (2026-09-10, v4.21 lexical lane, w_lexical 0.10): recall@5
1.000 (was 0.971: q13 now served), MRR 0.901 (unchanged: q13 +0.5, q02 -0.5),
Hard re-marked per the re-selection rule: rr < 1.0 = q02 q06 q08 q13 q19 q33,
multi-hit = q14 → 7 queries, hard MRR 0.5048, minus 0.5/7 = 0.0714 → 0.433.
q02 is the lane's one cost: 'windows workstation' matches the machine memory
word for word, so it now edges the ssh memory that answers the question.
Two caveats on the hard floor (review, 2026-09-02): the 0.0833 step is
sourced entirely by q14, the only hard query at rr 1.0 — the other five
can each lose at most 0.033-0.167. And the hard set is frozen against the
E1 ranker's own outcomes; a ranker that fixes q33 while breaking a
currently-easy query clears the hard gate. RE-SELECTION RULE: whenever the
primary floors are re-baselined, re-mark hard = every query with rr < 1.0
under the new baseline plus every multi-hit query, re-measure, re-floor.

memories.summary: Anvil is the Ubuntu laptop that acts as the launchpad; the coding agent Quill runs there.
Bellows is the Windows workstation with the RTX 4070; it hosts the memory server on port 51001, reachable only over the mesh VPN.
SSH into Bellows as user smith over the mesh VPN address 203.0.113.9; the old LAN address 192.0.2.6 died after the board swap.
The machine called Forge was decommissioned in June and wiped; every reference to forge:PORT is dead and must not be routed to.
Pip is the desk agent running on Anvil with its web dashboard on localhost port 3101.
The message bus is SQLite plus HTTP on port 50090; the chat mirror in Discord is display only and the owner is the bell.
Nightly rsync backs Anvil up to Bellows at 02:30; the memory corpus also goes offsite to a cloud bucket at 03:35.
Doctrine: archive before anything destructive. Copy aside first, delete last, never rewrite a file from memory.
Doctrine: a live credential is revoked, never archived; a backup copy keeps the exposure alive.
Doctrine: when the brain files and the memory server disagree, the brain files win; brain is now, memory is then.
Doctrine: scream on failure. If something breaks, say so loudly; silent degradation is forbidden.
Doctrine: git add names specific paths, never -A or dot; a pre-commit hook blocks the wildcard forms.
Doctrine: an HTTP 200 is not health; read the response body before declaring a service up.
Doctrine: an untested capability is a claim, not a capability; fire every trap after a restart or deploy.
Incident: Anvil froze hard on the 24th and had to be power cycled; the journal ended with no error, so the cause is undetermined.
Incident: the second Anvil lockup showed a wedged discrete GPU with 29 modeset errors in the last two minutes; the failing 3060 is the suspect.
Incident: pkill -f with a pattern that matches your own shell kills the shell; use pkill -x with the command name instead.
Incident: a PowerShell script shipped to Bellows failed to parse because of a non-ASCII dash; PowerShell 5 reads BOM-less UTF-8 as ANSI.
Incident: the updater reported restarted but had restarted a sidecar; the main gateway process kept its old start timestamp.
The owner is a retired maker who prints small seasonal collectibles; not a developer of modern stacks, but deep computing roots.
Quill is second in command under the owner and the de facto project manager; opinions are wanted, not just execution.
Mara is the owner's daughter; she sells succulents and was the first advertising client, and she is done with her web store as of August.
Dorian is a high school friend reconnected after decades, a machinist and photographer whose pictures fill the training gallery.
Cal is a blues drummer collaborating on a 3D printed drummers multi-tool with a drum key and a 7/16 inch socket.
Decision: the gallery is free plus donations, not a store; the owner killed selling in July and never wants monetization proposed again.
Decision: the coding agent runs the top tier model daily; conserve by lean sessions, not by dropping tiers.
Decision: security notices route to the coding agent first for triage; the Windows coder executes exact work orders.
Decision: art using third party characters is always free and unwatermarked, never priced.
Decision: the recall ranker anchors similarity on the pool's best hit over a fixed span of 0.20 cosine, after the raw term proved inert.
Current state: Pip's agent framework is one release behind; the upgrade is gated on the owner's word.
Current state: 48 operating system security updates are pending on Anvil, waiting on the owner.
Current state: the memory library's launch promotion on social media ends around the second of the month.
Current state: the PDF library was upgraded to 6.16.2 after three advisories; the next scan should clear it.
Idea: a documentary cut from the pre-2025 chat archive, cross referenced against the memory corpus, with the owner as tiebreaker.
Idea: a voice library of the owner's stories, recorded in short takes and indexed by the memory server.
Idea: a memory stick that carries a lane's facts between machines, syncing facts but never vector geometry.
Session log: ran the test suite, 724 passed, pushed the branch, updated the lane file.
Session log: checked the bus inbox, empty; read the security digest; nothing owed.
The dashboard for the experimental Windows desk agent listens on port 18789 on Bellows; a test bed only.
Hourly local backup of Pip's workspace runs on Anvil; it is separate from the nightly rsync.
Incident: years ago the old desktop froze weekly because of a bad power supply; replaced, closed.
The archive helper script names and ledgers each copy it makes under the archive directory.
Current state: Bellows answers on the LAN address 192.0.2.6.
